html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Set out the business context and use case for an AI system
  • Carry out or review an impact assessment
  • Apply policies, best practices and ethics to design and build
  • Identify and manage risks with matrices, hierarchies, benchmarks and pilots
  • Document the design and build to show compliance and manage risk

2III.A.1: Establish why the system is needed and what it will be used for

Exam angle

The BoK verb is Define, so the depth is Remember. The course has 1 practice question on this indicator.

Running case

A Ratio of 0.68 Before Launch

  • Lucia Moreno wants the hiring tool live for the next campaign
  • Daniel Osei, Head of Data Science, runs the impact assessment: the tool selects women at 68% of the rate of men, an impact ratio of 0.68
  • That is below the usual 0.8 rule-of-thumb threshold
  • Samira Haddad asks: approve with conditions, fix first, or stop?

The Business Context and the Use Case

  • Purpose and objectives: the problem and the decision the system will support
  • Users and affected people: who operates it, and who is subject to its outputs
  • Benefits and success criteria: how success is measured, including harm limits
  • Constraints and risk tolerance: data, cost, time, and the risk the organization accepts
  • Legal and ethical context: laws, standards and values that apply
  • Alternatives: including a non-AI option

Exam tip: Governance starts before design: no clear purpose, no meaningful risk assessment.

Is AI the Right Tool?

  • State the problem before the solution
  • List alternatives, including rules, process change or a simpler method
  • Compare benefit, cost and risk; NIST asks users to weigh viable non-AI alternatives (MANAGE 2.1)
  • Decide: go, no-go or go with conditions; the mapping work should give enough context for an initial go or no-go decision
  • Record the reasoning

Exam tip: If a simpler non-AI method meets the need with less risk, the governance answer may be not to use AI.

Approving the Use Case: Gate, Owner and Conditions

  • A use case passes the intake gate (module 3) with a named business owner, a risk tier, and the required sign-offs
  • Helios: Lucia Moreno owns the hiring tool; the committee tiers it high-risk and asks for an impact assessment first
  • Approval can carry conditions: tests that must pass, controls that must exist, a review date
  • The approval is recorded, with the context assumptions it rests on
  • If the context changes (a new region, a new use), the use case is re-approved

Exam tip: Approval with conditions is normal; the conditions must be specific, owned and checked.

3III.A.2: Carry out or review an impact assessment

Exam angle

The BoK verb is Perform, so the depth is Apply. The course has 2 practice questions on this indicator.

Impact Assessments Compared Beyond the BoK

  • DPIA: GDPR Article 35; risk to people's rights from processing personal data; needed before processing likely to be high risk
  • Fundamental rights impact assessment: AI Act Article 27; certain deployers of high-risk systems; before first use; may cross-refer to a DPIA
  • AI system impact assessment: ISO/IEC 42005 guidance; effects on individuals and society across the life cycle; any organization
  • Algorithmic impact assessment: the effects of automated decisions, in policy and some laws
  • They overlap: do the work once, and cross-reference it

Exam tip: The assessments overlap, so the usual answer is to build one on another rather than repeat the work.

Performing an AI Impact Assessment

  • Scope the system, its intended and foreseeable uses
  • Identify the people and groups affected, including vulnerable groups
  • Analyze benefits and harms: likelihood, severity and bias metrics
  • Set mitigations with owners and dates
  • Approve with conditions, signed by the accountable owner
  • Monitor and reassess when anything material changes

Exam tip: The assessment's point is to inform a decision, so its output is a recommendation with conditions.

Measuring Impact: The Impact Ratio at Helios

  • Impact ratio = the selection rate of one group divided by the rate of the highest group
  • Before the fix: women were selected at 68% of the rate of men, a ratio of 0.68, below 0.8
  • After the fix: the ratio is 0.91, above the threshold
  • A ratio above 0.8 does not prove the tool is lawful (module 5); it removes the red flag, and testing continues
  • Use several metrics, because no single number captures fairness

Exam tip: The ratio is the lower group's rate over the higher group's rate; under 0.8 means investigate.

Acting on the Findings

  • Find the cause: biased training data, a proxy feature, an unsuitable threshold, or a flawed label
  • Mitigate: remove or rebalance features, re-weight data, adjust thresholds, add human review, or change the design
  • Retest on fresh data and record the result
  • Decide with the accountable owner: approve with conditions, send back, or stop
  • Helios: the team removes proxy features and recalibrates; the ratio becomes 0.91; launch is approved with monitoring and a re-test after each hiring campaign
  • Keep the assessment on file as evidence

Exam tip: An assessment that finds a problem is a success; the failure is launching without acting on it.

4III.A.3: Apply policies, practices and ethics to the design and build

Exam angle

The BoK verb is Apply, so the depth is Apply. The course has 1 practice question on this indicator.

Governance by Design: The Design Stages

  • Apply policy, best practice and ethics at each design step
  • Purpose and requirements, data analysis, architecture and model selection
  • Human oversight, metrics and thresholds, stakeholder feedback, operational controls
  • Each step has a decision and a record
  • Late fixes cost more: design in fairness, explainability, privacy and safety

Exam tip: Questions about design ask which control belongs at which step.

Requirements Gathering and Model Selection

  • Functional requirements: what the system must do
  • Responsible-AI requirements: fairness targets, explainability level, privacy and security needs, safety and reliability limits, oversight points
  • Requirements are testable and traceable to the use case and the risks
  • Data analysis: check the data's quality, balance and fit for the purpose before choosing a model
  • Model selection weighs accuracy, interpretability, data needs, cost, security and the build, buy or fine-tune choice
  • Record the options considered and why one was chosen

Exam tip: A more accurate but opaque model is not automatically the right choice; the use case sets the balance.

Designing Human Oversight

  • In the loop: a person approves each decision; fits high-stakes individual decisions
  • On the loop: a person monitors and can intervene; fits high-volume, lower-stakes work
  • In command: a person decides whether and how the system is used
  • Whatever the mode, design time, information, training and authority to override (module 6, Article 14)
  • Guard against automation bias: show reasons and uncertainty, and log overrides
  • Helios: a recruiter reviews every rejection the tool recommends

Exam tip: Oversight that cannot change the outcome is for show; design the override.

Metrics and Thresholds

Kind Examples Why it matters
Performance accuracy, precision, recall, error rates does it work for the purpose
Fairness selection rates and impact ratio, error rates by group does it treat groups equitably
Robustness and safety performance on unusual or adversarial inputs does it hold up
Explainability whether reasons can be given to users can it be overseen and contested
  • Set the thresholds before testing: the acceptance criteria for launch and for later monitoring
  • The AI Act asks for testing before market placement against predefined metrics and probabilistic thresholds (Article 9)
  • Trade-offs between metrics are decided by the owner, openly

Exam tip: Thresholds set after seeing the results are not governance; set them first.

Stakeholder Engagement, Feedback and Operational Controls

  • Engage stakeholders: users, affected groups, legal, privacy, security and the business, early and repeatedly
  • Collect feedback in design reviews and pilots, and record what changed because of it
  • Operational controls designed in: access control, logging, monitoring hooks, change management, a way to pause or stop
  • Security by design: threat modeling and protection of data and model
  • Hand-off: the design carries operating instructions for the deployer

Exam tip: A system that cannot be logged, monitored or stopped was not designed for governance.

5III.A.4: Find and manage the risks of designing and building

Exam angle

The BoK verb is Identify, so the depth is Understand. The course has 2 practice questions on this indicator.

Internal and External Risk Factors

  • Internal factors: data quality and bias, model choice and complexity, skills and capacity, process and approval gaps
  • External factors: laws and regulators, vendors and the supply chain, attackers and misuse, social and market context
  • Risks interact: a weak vendor and poor data can combine
  • Identify risks to people as well as to the organization

Exam tip: A complete risk review looks both inward and outward.

The Probability and Severity Harms Matrix

  • Rate each risk by probability and severity
  • High-high risks come first; low-low risks are accepted or monitored
  • Consider severity to people (rights, safety, livelihood), not only cost
  • Low-probability, high-severity harms still need controls
  • Helios: a biased ranking is medium probability and high severity, so it gets the strongest controls

Exam tip: A harms matrix ranks; it does not decide acceptance by itself, since the owner sets the risk tolerance.

The Risk Mitigation Hierarchy

  • First: eliminate the risk through design (remove the feature, the data or the use)
  • Second: mitigate and control (technical safeguards, thresholds, human oversight)
  • Third: inform and train (instructions, warnings, deployer training)
  • Then: judge the residual risk acceptable, documented and approved
  • The AI Act's risk management duty states this same order (Article 9)

Exam tip: A warning or training is the weakest answer when the risk can be designed out.

Stakeholder Mapping, Use-Case Evaluation and Benchmarking

  • Stakeholder mapping: list everyone affected or interested, their influence and stake, and how each will be consulted
  • Use-case evaluation: test the use case against ethics, law and risk tolerance, and re-evaluate when it changes
  • Benchmarking: compare performance and risk with standard test sets, similar systems and human baselines
  • Internal and external review: a second pair of eyes from legal, security and independent experts
  • Record findings in the risk register with owners

Exam tip: Mapping the people affected is how a design team finds harms it would otherwise miss.

Pre-Deployment Pilots and Testing

  • Pilots run the system on a limited scale to learn before full launch
  • Shadow mode: the system runs without acting, so its outputs are compared with human decisions
  • Phased rollout: a small group first, then wider, with stop criteria
  • Testing: performance, fairness, robustness, security and red-team exercises
  • Go or no-go criteria are set in advance, and the decision is recorded
  • The AI Act allows testing in real-world conditions under defined safeguards (Articles 9 and 60)

Exam tip: A pilot is a controlled test with exit criteria, not a soft launch with no way back.

6III.A.5: Document how the system was designed and built

Exam angle

The BoK verb is Document, so the depth is Apply. The course has 1 practice question on this indicator.

Documenting the Design and Build

  • Why document: to show compliance and manage risk: auditors, regulators and later teams rely on it
  • What: the use case and approval, impact assessment, requirements, design decisions and alternatives, risk register, data sources, test plan and results, approvals and versions
  • Keep it version-controlled, dated and owned
  • Write it as you go; reconstructing it later is unreliable
  • Helios: the design record is the file Samira Haddad's committee reviews at the launch gate

Exam tip: If it is not documented, an auditor cannot tell whether it was done.

Documentation for Compliance: Annex IV and Model Records Beyond the BoK

  • The AI Act's technical documentation (Article 11, Annex IV) is the model for a high-risk design record
  • Annex IV, first part: a general description; the development process (methods, design specifications and trade-offs, architecture, data requirements, human oversight assessment, pre-determined changes, validation and testing with metrics, cybersecurity)
  • Annex IV, second part: monitoring and control; justification of metrics; the risk management system; lifecycle changes; standards applied; the declaration of conformity (Article 47); the post-market monitoring plan (Article 72)
  • Testing logs and reports are dated and signed
  • Model cards and datasheets summarize a model and its data (module 9)

Exam tip: Documentation is a continuing record: it must be updated when the design changes.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (one best answer, or select exactly the number the question asks for)

S1Lucia Moreno asks what must be settled about the business context before the hiring tool is designed. Which set is the best answer?

  • AThe model architecture, the hyperparameters and the cloud vendor to be used for training
  • BThe final test results, the launch date and the exact wording of the candidate notice text
  • CThe advertising message, the price of the service and the expected number of paying customers
  • DPurpose, users and people affected, success criteria, constraints and any non-AI alternative
Show the answer

Answer: D. A use case defines the purpose, the users and affected people, the benefits and success criteria, the constraints and the alternatives, including a non-AI option. Architecture, results and marketing come later or belong elsewhere.

S2Before launch, Helios's hiring tool selects women at 68% of the rate of men. What should Helios conclude and do?

  • ALaunch as planned, because recruiters make the final decision about each applicant
  • BTreat the ratio of 0.68 as acceptable, because it is above the four-fifths threshold of 0.8 in use
  • CTreat 0.68 as a red flag below 0.8, find the cause, mitigate, retest and decide before launch
  • DDelete the assessment from the file, because a poor result should not be kept as evidence
Show the answer

Answer: C. A ratio of 0.68 is below the 0.8 rule of thumb, so it is a signal of possible adverse impact. The team should find the cause, mitigate, retest and decide before launch, and keep the assessment on file.

S3Which TWO statements about impact assessments are correct? (Select TWO.)

  • AAn AI impact assessment replaces the need for a data protection impact assessment
  • BA fundamental rights impact assessment is required for AI systems used in commercial sectors
  • CA DPIA is required under GDPR Article 35 for processing likely to be high risk to people
  • DISO/IEC 42005 is a binding regulation that fixes the exact format of assessment reports
  • EA fundamental rights assessment can cross-refer to an existing DPIA to avoid duplication
Show the answer

Answer: C, E. Article 35 requires a DPIA for processing likely to be high risk, and the AI Act lets a deployer's fundamental rights impact assessment cross-refer to a DPIA. An AI impact assessment does not replace a DPIA, the rights assessment is required only of certain deployers, and ISO/IEC 42005 is guidance.

S4A team is designing a hiring tool. Which TWO practices best apply governance to the design stage? (Select TWO.)

  • AChoosing the largest available model, whatever the effect on the ability to explain results
  • BDesigning human oversight with the time, information and authority to override the tool
  • CCollecting the widest range of data fields about applicants in case it improves the model
  • DSetting fairness and performance thresholds before testing begins and recording them
  • ESkipping stakeholder feedback during design to shorten the schedule before the pilot
Show the answer

Answer: B, D. Oversight must be designed with real authority to override, and thresholds are set before testing so that results cannot move the goalposts. Choosing size over explainability, collecting everything and skipping feedback work against governance.

S5On a probability and severity harms matrix, which risk should the team treat first?

  • AA harm with a high probability and a high severity for the people affected by the system
  • BA harm with a low probability and a low severity that would cost very little to fix later
  • CA harm that has a high probability but a negligible effect on the people affected
  • DA harm that is expensive for the company but unlikely to affect the people involved
Show the answer

Answer: A. The matrix ranks risks by probability and severity, so a high-high risk to people takes priority. Low-low risks can be accepted or monitored, and cost to the company is not the only measure of severity.

S6During design review, a team finds a feature that can produce harmful outputs. Under the risk mitigation hierarchy, which response is the most preferred?

  • AAdd a warning about the feature to the user guide and the release notes for deployers
  • BTrain the deployers to recognize when the feature produces harmful outputs and to escalate
  • CAdd a monitoring alert that notifies the operations team when harmful outputs are detected
  • DRedesign the system to remove the cause, so the harmful outputs cannot occur at all
Show the answer

Answer: D. The hierarchy prefers eliminating the risk through design, then mitigation and control, then information and training. A warning, training or an alert are less effective than removing the cause.

S7Which design-stage record best helps show compliance and manage risk for a high-risk system?

  • AA slide deck shown at the kickoff meeting, saved on one team member's own laptop for later
  • BA version-controlled design record of use case, assessment, requirements, risks, tests and approvals
  • CAn email thread among the developers that mentions the main decisions and some of the known risks
  • DA summary written from memory after launch, to be filed when an auditor eventually asks
Show the answer

Answer: B. A dated, owned and version-controlled record of the use case, assessment, requirements, alternatives, risks, tests and approvals shows what was done and why. Informal or after-the-fact records cannot reliably do that.
